questions.q: A 32-year-old pregnant woman presents with symmetrical brown patches on her forehead, cheeks, and upper lip with sparing of the philtrum and nasolabial folds. Wood's lamp examination shows enhancement of pigmentation. Which histopathological finding is most likely in this patient?
opts: Liquefaction degeneration of basal layer with pigmentary incontinence
Increased epidermal melanin with biologically active melanocytes
Horny plugs filling follicles with perivascular infiltrate
Band-like dermal infiltrate with normal epidermis
questions.exp: The clinical presentation is classic for centrofacial melasma (mask of pregnancy). Wood's lamp enhancement suggests epidermal melasma, which histopathologically shows increased epidermal melanin with melanocytes that are biologically more active compared to perilesional skin.

questions.q: A 28-year-old pregnant woman presents at 12 weeks gestation with a positive VDRL test and confirmed primary syphilis. She is concerned about the risk of transmission to her fetus. What is the approximate probability of vertical transmission of Treponema pallidum in primary syphilis?
questions.exp: The probability of transplacental transmission is highest during primary or secondary syphilis (70-100%) due to high concentrations of treponemes in maternal blood. Transmission rates decrease significantly in latent stages (40% for early latent, 10% for late latent).

questions.q: A surgeon is planning an elliptical excision on the forearm. The lesion is 8 mm in diameter. What should be the minimum length of the ellipse and maximum apex angle to prevent dog-ear formation?
questions.exp: The ellipse length-to-width ratio should be at least 3:1, making the minimum length 24 mm for an 8 mm lesion. The apex angle must be ≤30° to prevent dog-ear formation; angles greater than 30° lead to tissue redundancy at the wound ends.

questions.q: A 28-year-old farmer from Tamil Nadu presents with linear vesicular eruptions on his forearm after waking up in the morning. He recalls brushing off an insect from his arm while sleeping. The lesions appeared overnight with a burning sensation. Which of the following statements about the causative toxin is correct?
opts: It is a terpenoid compound synthesized by beetle salivary glands
It is produced by endosymbiotic Pseudomonas bacteria within the beetle's hemolymph
It acts by inhibiting protein phosphatases PP1 and PP2A
It requires the beetle to actively bite or sting the victim
questions.exp: The clinical scenario describes Paederus dermatitis caused by crushing of rove beetles against skin. Pederin, the vesicant toxin, is not synthesized by the beetle itself but by endosymbiotic Pseudomonas bacteria residing in the hemolymph. The toxin is released through reflex bleeding when the beetle is crushed.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with a painful, thick hyperkeratotic papule on the sole of his foot that developed over several months. On dermoscopy, multiple black dots are visible within the lesion, and the natural skin lines appear disrupted across the surface. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Plantar warts characteristically interrupt the natural dermatoglyphic skin lines and show thrombosed capillaries appearing as black dots on dermoscopy. In contrast, corns and calluses preserve skin markings and lack vascular puncta.

questions.q: A 19-year-old sexually inactive female presents with acute onset of painful, deep necrotic ulcers on the vulva. She has concurrent pharyngitis, fever, and cervical lymphadenopathy. Serological testing is most likely to reveal primary infection with which organism?
questions.exp: This presentation is classic for Lipschütz ulcers (ulcus vulvae acutum), which are non-sexually acquired acute genital ulcers predominantly occurring in young, sexually inactive women. They are strongly associated with primary Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) infection, often accompanied by infectious mononucleosis symptoms.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with a 6mm pigmented lesion on her back with irregular borders and color variegation. Dermoscopy reveals an atypical pigment network. Which biopsy technique is most appropriate for this lesion?
opts: 3mm punch biopsy from the darkest area
Incisional biopsy of the thickest portion
questions.exp: Excisional biopsy is the preferred technique for suspected melanoma as it allows complete margin assessment and accurate Breslow depth measurement. Shave and punch biopsies are contraindicated in suspected melanoma as they may compromise Breslow depth assessment or cause sampling error.

questions.q: In the pathogenesis of atopic dermatitis, which epithelial cell-derived cytokine initiates the Th2 differentiation pathway from naive T helper cells?
questions.exp: TSLP is a key epithelial cell-secreted cytokine that drives naive Th0 cells towards Th2 differentiation in atopic dermatitis. IL-4 and IL-13 are downstream Th2 effector cytokines, while IL-31 is primarily associated with pruritus.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with palpable purpura on bilateral lower extremities that appeared 10 days after starting amoxicillin for sinusitis. Skin biopsy shows fibrinoid necrosis of post-capillary venules with neutrophilic infiltrate and nuclear debris. What is the primary immunopathologic mechanism responsible for this condition?
questions.exp: Cutaneous small vessel vasculitis is primarily a Type III hypersensitivity reaction where circulating immune complexes deposit in post-capillary venule walls, activate complement, and recruit neutrophils that cause vessel damage through release of proteolytic enzymes.

questions.q: A stillborn infant at 32 weeks gestation is found to have congenital syphilis on autopsy. Which of the following histopathological findings is characteristic of this condition?
opts: Caseous necrosis with Langhans giant cells
Obliterative endarteritis with plasma cell infiltration
questions.exp: Congenital syphilis, like acquired syphilis, is histologically characterized by obliterative endarteritis with mononuclear and plasma cell infiltration surrounding blood vessels, along with intimal hyperplasia and swollen endothelial cells. Fibrosis and gummata may also be observed.

questions.q: Genomic studies of Mycosis Fungoides have revealed a prominent mutational signature suggesting which of the following as a major mutagenic factor in its pathogenesis?
questions.exp: High-throughput sequencing studies have revealed a prominent ultraviolet (UV) mutational signature in mycosis fungoides, suggesting UV radiation acts as a major mutagen before clonal expansion of the malignant T-cells.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man with discoid lupus erythematosus has lesions distributed on the face, scalp, arms, and trunk. What is the approximate risk of this patient developing systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)?
questions.exp: Generalized or disseminated DLE, defined as involvement beyond the neck region, carries a 20% risk of developing SLE. In contrast, localized DLE (involvement primarily above the neck) has only a 5% risk of SLE progression.

questions.q: A dermatologist is lecturing on blister beetle dermatitis. Which combination correctly pairs the beetle family with its characteristic toxin and mechanism of human exposure?
opts: Oedemeridae – Pederin – Attracted to light and bites at night
questions.exp: Paederus beetles belong to family Staphylinidae and produce pederin. They do not bite or sting but release the toxin when crushed against the skin through reflex bleeding. Meloidae family beetles produce cantharidin, not pederin.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with multiple smooth, firm, pink nodules coalescing over her scalp, giving a 'turban-like' appearance. Biopsy shows basaloid cell nests arranged in a jigsaw puzzle pattern surrounded by thick hyaline material. Which gene mutation is most likely responsible for this condition?
questions.exp: The clinical description of 'turban tumor' and histopathology showing jigsaw puzzle pattern with hyaline basement membrane is pathognomonic of cylindroma. Cylindromas are caused by loss-of-function mutations in the CYLD tumor suppressor gene located on chromosome 16q12-q13, which normally inhibits NF-κB signaling.

questions.q: A 32-year-old man with chronic plaque psoriasis shows histopathology revealing collections of neutrophils in the stratum corneum. Which chemokine is MOST directly responsible for attracting these neutrophils to form Munro microabscesses?
questions.exp: IL-8 (CXCL8) is a potent neutrophil chemoattractant that plays a key role in recruiting neutrophils to the epidermis in psoriasis, leading to the formation of Munro microabscesses. CCL17 and CCL27 primarily attract lymphocytes, while eotaxin attracts eosinophils.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman using multiple cosmetic products develops rapidly progressive grayish-brown pigmentation on her forehead and temples that extends to her neck. Early histopathology would most likely reveal:
opts: Liquefaction degeneration of basal layer with pigmentary incontinence
Epidermal melanin increase without dermal changes
questions.exp: This presentation is consistent with Riehl's melanosis (pigmented contact dermatitis) caused by cosmetics. Early histopathological features include liquefaction degeneration of the basal layer of epidermis, perivascular dermal infiltrate, and pigmentary incontinence.

questions.q: A dermatologist performs a 2mm punch biopsy on a patient with suspected bullous pemphigoid for direct immunofluorescence. What is the most appropriate wound management after this procedure?
opts: Primary layered closure with deep and superficial sutures
Application of hemostatic agent and suture closure
questions.exp: Punch biopsies of 3mm or smaller can heal adequately by secondary intention without sutures. Sutures are typically required for punch biopsies of 4mm or larger to achieve primary closure and optimal cosmesis.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with fixed, well-demarcated erythematous patches on his trunk and buttocks that have been slowly progressive over 3 years. Skin biopsy shows epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes with a CD3+, CD4+, CD8- immunophenotype. The localized nature of his disease is best explained by the derivation of neoplastic cells from which T-cell subset?
questions.exp: Mycosis fungoides is derived from non-recirculating Tissue-Resident Memory T-cells (TRM), which explains its presentation as fixed, localized patches and plaques in the skin. In contrast, Sézary syndrome derives from Central Memory T-cells (TCM) that recirculate, causing generalized erythroderma and leukemia.

questions.q: According to the SPUR criteria for suspecting primary immunodeficiency, which of the following presentations would be classified as 'Unusual'?
opts: Streptococcal pharyngitis in a school-going child
Aspergillus brain abscess in an otherwise healthy infant
questions.exp: The 'U' in SPUR refers to Unusual infections - those caused by opportunistic organisms or occurring at atypical sites. Aspergillus brain abscess in an immunocompetent infant is highly unusual and warrants immunodeficiency workup.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with purulent urethral discharge. Gram stain of the discharge reveals gram-negative diplococci within polymorphonuclear leukocytes. Which virulence factor of the causative organism prevents phagolysosome fusion and enables intracellular survival within neutrophils?
questions.exp: PorB is the major outer membrane porin of Neisseria gonorrhoeae that translocates into eukaryotic cell membranes and prevents phagolysosome fusion, activation, and degranulation inside neutrophils, enabling intracellular survival. It also mediates serum resistance by interfering with complement activation.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man presents with a suspected melanoma on his back. Which biopsy technique is most appropriate for initial evaluation?
opts: 4 mm punch biopsy from the darkest area
Incisional biopsy from the lesion edge
questions.exp: Excisional biopsy is the preferred technique for suspected melanoma as it allows complete histopathological assessment including accurate Breslow depth measurement. Shave biopsy is contraindicated as it compromises Breslow depth evaluation, and punch biopsy carries sampling error risk.

questions.q: The outer membrane of Neisseria gonorrhoeae contains lipo-oligosaccharide (LOS) instead of lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Which modification of LOS provides the gonococcus with resistance to complement-dependent bactericidal activity of normal human serum?
questions.exp: Sialylation of LOS, which hijacks host CMP-NANA, provides Neisseria gonorrhoeae with profound resistance to complement-dependent bactericidal action of normal human serum. This enables bacterial survival and dissemination into the bloodstream.

questions.q: A 32-year-old HIV-positive male presents with painful vesicular eruptions in a dermatomal distribution on the trunk, along with seborrhoeic dermatitis on the face and scalp. He has no fever or significant weight loss. According to the WHO Clinical Staging, which stage does this patient belong to?
questions.exp: Herpes zoster and seborrhoeic dermatitis are characteristic features of WHO Clinical Stage 2 (Mild) HIV disease. Stage 2 also includes papular pruritic eruptions, angular cheilitis, and fungal nail infections without severe systemic manifestations.

questions.q: A 40-year-old HIV-positive patient has a CD4 count of 45 cells/µL. Which of the following opportunistic infections is this patient at highest risk of developing?
questions.exp: CMV retinitis typically occurs at CD4 counts <50 cells/µL, indicating profound immune depletion. While PCP risk increases below 200 cells/µL and oral candidiasis below 500 cells/µL, CMV disease specifically manifests at the most severe immunosuppression level.

questions.q: A 32-year-old man presents with a single, indurated genital ulcer that is non-tender. On examination, bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy is noted. Which characteristic best differentiates this condition from chancroid?
questions.exp: The primary chancre of syphilis classically presents as a solitary, indurated, and painless ulcer, whereas chancroid typically presents with painful ulcers having ragged, undermined edges with purulent exudate. Pain assessment is a critical clinical differentiating feature between these two conditions.

questions.q: A patient with Brooke-Spiegler syndrome undergoes genetic testing revealing a CYLD gene mutation. What is the normal function of the protein encoded by this gene?
questions.exp: The CYLD gene encodes a deubiquitinating enzyme (ubiquitin hydrolase) that negatively regulates the NF-κB and JNK signaling pathways. Loss of CYLD function leads to uncontrolled NF-κB activation, resulting in anti-apoptotic signaling and tumor proliferation.

questions.q: According to the 2012 Revised International Chapel Hill Consensus Conference nomenclature, cutaneous leukocytoclastic angiitis is classified under which category when there is no evidence of systemic involvement?
questions.exp: Under the CHCC2012 nomenclature, cutaneous small vessel vasculitis (cutaneous leukocytoclastic angiitis) is classified as a single-organ vasculitis when there is no evidence of systemic vasculitis or involvement of other organs.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with well-defined erythematous plaques on her face and scalp. On examination, there is adherent scaling, and when the scale is removed, keratotic spikes are observed on its undersurface. The lesions show central atrophic scarring with peripheral hyperpigmentation. Which clinical sign is being described by the keratotic spikes on the undersurface of the scale?
questions.exp: The 'carpet-tack sign' or 'tin-tack sign' refers to keratotic spikes seen on the undersurface of scales in discoid lupus erythematosus (DLE), which correspond to follicular plugging. This is a characteristic clinical finding in classic DLE.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with recurrent pneumonia (4 episodes in the past year), persistent oral thrush despite treatment, and a serious episode of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia. Which mnemonic helps identify warning signs suggesting primary immunodeficiency in this patient?
questions.exp: SPUR stands for Serious, Persistent, Unusual, and Recurrent infections - the cardinal warning signs of primary immunodeficiency. This child demonstrates all four components with serious PCP infection, persistent candidiasis, unusual pathogen, and recurrent pneumonias.

questions.q: A patient presents with multiple coalescent, superficial hyperkeratotic plaques on the plantar surface that have been resistant to multiple treatment modalities. Which HPV type is most likely responsible for this presentation?
questions.exp: HPV-2 is classically associated with mosaic warts, which present as localized coalescent collections of multiple superficial plaques that are notoriously difficult to treat. HPV-1 is typically associated with deep, solitary endophytic warts (myrmecia).
